all_quotes.quote: SALVAGE has a higher propensity for starburst and green valley galaxies, probably because PIs are more likely to propose for extreme populations rather than representative samples.

The redshift of each target in SALVAGE determines the physical size of the inner region probed by the 3" SDSS fibre, which is shown along the top axis of the left panel. The radii of the central region probed by the SDSS fibre size ranges from $\thicksim$0.5-6 kpc, with a median of 1.3 kpc.

all_quotes.loc: On the assumption of a constant $\alpha_{CO}$
all_quotes.quote: Second, the “edge” of the outer region is not well-defined for each galaxy and can cause significant uncertainty in $\Sigma_{\star,\text{outer}}$. Lastly, the metallicity measurements from SDSS are based on emission lines that apply to the area within the fibre only.
Moreover, we are able to do so using purely archival data from SDSS and ALMA.

The reduced ALMA cubes, moment maps, and higher-order products that were produced by the SALVAGE project are available at <https://www.canfar.net/storage/vault/list/AstroDataCitationDOI/CISTI.CANFAR/25.0077/data>.

The PHANGS-ALMA imaging pipeline is available at <https://github.com/akleroy/phangs_imaging_scripts>, and the SALVAGE implementation of this pipeline, along with tutorials for interacting with the data, is available at <https://github.com/sj-wilkinson/SALVAGE>.
